title: Who Winds the Spring?
endLine: Oxidation pays for NADH and the thioester; the rest makes it one-way.

scenes.tts: Last time, one pyruvate entered a swinging-arm complex and left as acetyl co-A, carbon dioxide and NADH. That acetyl co-A leaves as a wound spring. Yet no ATP went in. So who wound it?
scenes.narration: Last time, one pyruvate entered a swinging-arm complex and left as acetyl-CoA, carbon dioxide and NADH. That acetyl-CoA leaves as a wound spring. Yet no ATP went in. So who wound it?
scenes.caption: Last time, one pyruvate entered a swinging-arm complex and left as acetyl-CoA, carbon dioxide and NADH. That acetyl-CoA leaves as a wound spring. Yet no ATP went in. So who wound it?
scenes.visual: COLOUR BY CONCEPT, carried from the first film: carbon cargo (pyruvate, acetyl group) YELLOW; acetyl-CoA GREEN; electrons and NADH ORANGE; enzymes and the complex BLUE; coenzymes (lipoamide arm, CoA) PINK; carbon dioxide, axes and structure GREY; 'blocked / not allowed' RED; ATP PURPLE. New in this film: the energy-level marker is a WHITE ball; the ordinary oxygen ester is CYAN; water drops are WHITE. WORLD, kept all film: at LEFT 35% of the frame, the first film's complex, rebuilt the same way but smaller: a BLUE round E2 core with BLUE E1 (upper left) and E3 (upper right) ellipses, a PINK lipoamide arm tethered to the core. At RIGHT 60%, an empty energy ledger, about 75% of frame height: vertical axis 'free energy (kJ/mol)' from +10 at top to -60 at bottom, ticks every 10, a WHITE ball resting on a short GREY shelf at 0 labelled 'pyruvate'. Small tag under the axis: 'standard values, pH 7'. Recap motion on the first sentence: a YELLOW 'pyruvate' chip enters the complex from the left, the PINK arm swings E1 to E2 to E3 once, and three chips leave: GREEN 'acetyl-CoA' to the right, ORANGE 'NADH' downward, a GREY 'CO2' bubble drifting up. On 'wound spring', a tight GREEN coil spring appears on the GREEN acetyl-CoA chip and quivers. On 'no ATP went in', a PURPLE 'ATP' chip slides toward the complex's entrance and is turned back with a RED cross; it fades. On the question, white text across the top: 'Who wound the spring?'

Title 'Who Winds the Spring?' fades in above the complex for 2 s while the question text fades out. The GREEN spring on the acetyl-CoA chip keeps quivering; the PINK arm drifts slowly; the WHITE ball rests at 0 on the ledger.

scenes.tts: To find out, keep the energy books. Pyruvate starts at zero, in kilojoules per mole. Downhill releases energy, and uphill spends it. We list three entries, not in the order they happen.
scenes.narration: To find out, keep the energy books. Pyruvate starts at zero, in kilojoules per mole. Downhill releases energy, and uphill spends it. We list three entries, not in the order they happen.
scenes.caption: To find out, keep the energy books. Pyruvate starts at zero, in kilojoules per mole. Downhill releases energy, and uphill spends it. We list three entries, not in the order they happen.
scenes.visual: The ledger at right brightens and the complex at left dims to 60% (still drifting). On 'downhill', a faint WHITE ghost ball rolls a short way down from 0 with a GREY down-arrow labelled 'energy released'; on 'uphill', a ghost rolls up with an up-arrow labelled 'energy spent'; both ghosts fade. On 'three entries', three empty slots appear along the ledger's horizontal axis, left to right; a tag above them reads 'ledger order, not reaction order'.

scenes.tts: First entry: the oxidation. Two carbons go from aldehyde level to acid level. Their electrons end on NAD plus. That falls about fifty kilojoules per mole.
scenes.narration: First entry: the oxidation. Two carbons go from aldehyde level to acid level. Their electrons end on NAD⁺. That falls about 50 kJ/mol.
scenes.caption: First entry: the oxidation. Two carbons go from aldehyde level to acid level. Their electrons end on NAD⁺. That falls about 50 kJ/mol.
scenes.visual: In the complex at left, the YELLOW two-carbon chip glows at E1 and an ORANGE pair of dots ('2 e-') travels along the PINK arm to E3 and into an ORANGE 'NADH' chip. In step with it, in slot one of the ledger, a thick ORANGE downward arrow grows from 0 to -50 and the WHITE ball rides down it to a shelf at -50. Label beside the arrow: 'oxidation ~ -50'. The ball rocks gently on its shelf.

scenes.tts: Second entry: the acetyl group is stored as a thioester on coenzyme A, not set free as acetate. That costs about thirty-one, uphill. It spends most of the oxidation's fifty.
scenes.narration: Second entry: the acetyl group is stored as a thioester on coenzyme A, not set free as acetate. That costs about 31, uphill. It spends most of the oxidation's 50.
scenes.caption: Second entry: the acetyl group is stored as a thioester on coenzyme A, not set free as acetate. That costs about 31, uphill. It spends most of the oxidation's 50.
scenes.visual: At left, the YELLOW acetyl chip snaps onto a PINK 'CoA' chip and becomes the GREEN 'acetyl-CoA' chip; a faint ghost 'free acetate' chip beside it is crossed out and fades. In slot two of the ledger, a thick GREEN upward arrow grows from -50 to -19 and the WHITE ball is carried up to a shelf at -19. Label: 'thioester ~ +31'. As the GREEN arrow rises, the GREEN spring on the acetyl-CoA chip winds visibly tighter, coil by coil, in step with the arrow. On 'most of the oxidation's fifty', a GREEN bracket spans 31 of the ORANGE arrow's 50 units (from -50 up to -19).

scenes.tts: Third entry: carbon dioxide leaves, about fourteen more downhill. That one is found by difference, so it is approximate. Add them up: minus fifty, plus thirty-one, minus fourteen. About minus thirty-three overall.
scenes.narration: Third entry: carbon dioxide leaves, about 14 more downhill. That one is found by difference, so it is approximate. Add them up: −50, +31, −14. About −33 overall.
scenes.caption: Third entry: carbon dioxide leaves, about 14 more downhill. That one is found by difference, so it is approximate. Add them up: −50, +31, −14. About −33 overall.
scenes.visual: At left, the GREY 'CO2' bubble rises out of the complex and drifts away. In slot three of the ledger, a GREY downward arrow grows from -19 to -33 and the WHITE ball rolls down to a shelf at -33. Label: 'lose CO2 ~ -14'; under it a small tag 'by difference, approx.'. On 'add them up', a running sum appears at the top of the ledger in white: '-50 + 31 - 14 = -33'. A WHITE bracket on the left of the ledger spans 0 to -33, labelled 'overall ~ -33'.

scenes.tts: So here is the answer. The oxidation is the main energy source. It pays for the NADH and for the thioester. What is left, together with losing carbon dioxide, makes the gate one-way.
scenes.narration: So here is the answer. The oxidation is the main energy source. It pays for the NADH and for the thioester. What is left, together with losing carbon dioxide, makes the gate one-way.
scenes.caption: So here is the answer. The oxidation is the main energy source. It pays for the NADH and for the thioester. What is left, together with losing carbon dioxide, makes the gate one-way.
scenes.visual: All three ledger arrows stay. On 'main energy source', the ORANGE arrow pulses. On 'the NADH', the ORANGE NADH chip at left pulses; on 'the thioester', the GREEN arrow and the GREEN spring pulse together. On 'what is left', the top segment of the ORANGE arrow, from 0 down to -19 (the 19 units of the oxidation's 50 that the thioester did not use), glows, and the GREY CO2 arrow glows with it; both slide into the WHITE 'overall ~ -33' bracket. A label appears under the ledger: 'leftover + CO2 = one-way'.

scenes.tts: How one-way? A drop of about thirty-three gives an equilibrium constant near four hundred thousand at body temperature. In practice, the reaction runs only forward. In animals, no enzyme runs it backward.
scenes.narration: How one-way? A drop of about 33 gives an equilibrium constant near 4 × 10⁵ at body temperature. In practice, the reaction runs only forward. In animals, no enzyme runs it backward.
scenes.caption: How one-way? A drop of about 33 gives an equilibrium constant near 4 × 10⁵ at body temperature. In practice, the reaction runs only forward. In animals, no enzyme runs it backward.
scenes.visual: The ledger dims to 50%. At left, between the YELLOW pyruvate entrance and the GREEN acetyl-CoA exit of the complex, a thick GREEN forward arrow labelled 'forward' and a thin backward arrow appear. Text in white beside the arrows: 'K ~ 4 x 10^5 at 37 C' (computed from e^(33 / (0.0083 x 310)), about 3.6 x 10^5; show only the rounded lesson value). On 'only forward', YELLOW chips stream in and GREEN chips stream out through the forward arrow. On 'no enzyme runs it backward', the thin backward arrow is struck with a RED cross, and a GREEN acetyl-CoA chip that drifts back toward the entrance bounces off it. Small tag: 'in animals'.

scenes.tts: Now look at the spring itself. Picture two esters: an ordinary one, joined through oxygen, and this one, joined through sulfur. Split each with water. Which releases more energy?
scenes.narration: Now look at the spring itself. Picture two esters: an ordinary one, joined through oxygen, and this one, joined through sulfur. Split each with water. Which releases more energy?
scenes.caption: Now look at the spring itself. Picture two esters: an ordinary one, joined through oxygen, and this one, joined through sulfur. Split each with water. Which releases more energy?
scenes.visual: The ledger shrinks to a small inset at top right, still showing its three arrows. The complex slides to a small inset at top left. Centre stage, filling about 60% of frame height: two large chips side by side, CYAN 'oxygen ester' on the left and GREEN 'thioester' on the right, each with an identical coil spring (no difference shown yet). No molecular structures. A WHITE water drop labelled 'water' hovers over each. Question card across the top in white: 'Which releases more?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Both water drops bob slowly above their chips; both springs quiver identically. No other change.

scenes.tts: The sulfur one. The oxygen ester gives about twenty-one. The thioester gives about thirty-one, roughly matching ATP's thirty point five. That is the same thirty-one the oxidation paid to build it.
scenes.narration: The sulfur one. The oxygen ester gives about 21. The thioester gives about 31, roughly matching ATP's 30.5. That is the same 31 the oxidation paid to build it.
scenes.caption: The sulfur one. The oxygen ester gives about 21. The thioester gives about 31, roughly matching ATP's 30.5. That is the same 31 the oxidation paid to build it.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. Each water drop falls onto its chip and the spring releases. Below each chip a downward arrow grows on a shared small scale (0 to -35 kJ/mol, ticks every 5): CYAN to -21, labelled 'about -21'; GREEN to -31, labelled 'about -31'. A PURPLE dashed line at -30.5 runs across both, labelled 'ATP ~ -30.5'; the GREEN arrow ends just past it. On 'the same thirty-one', the inset ledger at top right enlarges briefly and its GREEN '+31' arrow pulses together with the GREEN '-31' arrow: one goes up, one comes down, equal length.

scenes.tts: Why? Not because energy hides in the bond. Breaking a bond always costs energy. Sulfur is larger than oxygen, so it overlaps the carbonyl carbon poorly. The thioester gets little resonance help. Its products, acetate and free coenzyme A, are much more stable. The thioester is a boulder perched on a cliff.

scenes.visual: Schematic, no molecular structures. On 'energy hides in the bond', a small white tag 'stored in the bond?' gets a RED cross. On 'Sulfur is larger', two plain discs appear: a large GREEN disc 'S' and a smaller CYAN disc 'O', each touching a GREY chip 'C=O'; the CYAN disc's contact glows strongly, the GREEN disc's contact glows faintly. On 'little resonance help', a two-bar gauge titled 'resonance help (schematic)' appears: CYAN bar long, GREEN bar short. On 'much more stable', the scene becomes a GREEN boulder labelled 'thioester' perched on a cliff edge at left, with a valley floor at right holding a YELLOW 'acetate' chip and a PINK 'CoA' chip; the boulder rolls off the cliff into the valley and settles, splitting into those two chips.

scenes.tts: So no ATP wound the spring. Oxidizing two carbons one notch further did, and it paid for the NADH too. Acetyl co-A carries that push into the citric acid cycle's first step, and into fatty-acid synthesis. What remained keeps the traffic one-way.

scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: complex at left, ledger at right with its three arrows and the WHITE ball at -33. On 'no ATP', the PURPLE ATP chip reappears at the entrance, crossed out, and fades. On 'two carbons one notch further', the ORANGE ledger arrow and the ORANGE NADH chip pulse. On 'citric acid cycle', the GREEN acetyl-CoA chip with its tight spring travels off to the right toward a GREEN-outlined token labelled 'citric acid cycle'; on 'fatty-acid synthesis', a second GREEN chip travels to a token labelled 'fatty-acid synthesis'. On 'one-way', YELLOW chips keep streaming in through the GREEN forward arrow; the RED-crossed backward arrow stays.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (YELLOW chips entering the complex, GREEN chips leaving, the PINK arm swinging, the WHITE ball resting at -33). Large white text, centred: 'Oxidation pays for NADH and the thioester; the rest makes it one-way.'
